points.text: Too few baselines; only DAPO besides GRPO.
Experimental analysis insufficient.
Scalability across model architectures or sizes not verified.
Only standard math benchmarks; no out-of-distribution tasks.
Core ideas (adaptive sampling, filtering, replay) already explored in prior work.
Evaluation only on math despite general-domain training data; general reasoning benchmarks missing.
Only Qwen2.5-7B backbones; transfer to Llama or Gemma untested.
Possible Qwen data contamination makes benchmark conclusions unreliable.
Gains of about 1% over baselines are small.
Max response length 2048 may impair baseline exploration compared to DAPO default.
Evaluation hyperparameters and training prompt template not reported.
Computational overhead of extra rollouts and replay not reported.
Framework mainly combines known components on GRPO rather than new principle.
Claim that numerous low-quality samples drown out high-quality signal is questionable.
Applicability of tabular NPG theorem to this setting unclear.
Experimental setting toy-like: older Qwen, 2k context, only 5 rollouts.
Evaluation protocol unclear; pass@1 on AIME high-variance, should use pass@k averaging.
MATH accuracies not multiples of 1/500, inconsistent with pass@1.
Figure 5 reward and accuracy trends contradict, possibly from evaluation variance.
DAPO performing worse than GRPO unexplained.
Typo: EFR should be EFRame in Figure 3.
Limited novelty; similar mechanisms in RLEP, RePO, VL-Rethinker.
No comparison against closely related replay/filtering methods.
Exploration improvement not supported by pass@k.
Only two Qwen models; other LLM families untested.
Newer reasoning benchmarks (AIME25, HMMT-Feb25, etc.) omitted.
Qwen2.5 data leakage risk raises doubts about improvements.
No theoretical explanation why combined design improves performance.
Results appear single-run with no seeds, variances, or confidence intervals.
Margins over GRPO and DAPO small and within noise; GRPO wins on MathVision.
Headline relative-gain percentages inflate small absolute improvements.
Method costs more compute per step; no compute-matched baseline.
Figure 1 group-size comparison is not the right comparison.
Missing baselines: dynamic sampling, curricula, off-policy guidance, prioritized replay.
DAPO baseline appears partially configured without dynamic sampling.
Only one 7B model, training mostly on Geo3K.
Unclear which training data produced the main results row.
Other baselines copied from papers with different settings; evaluation protocol unspecified.
Max response length 2048 short for deeper reasoning; length growth not evidence.
Deeper-reasoning claim untested: no pass@k, hard-prompt analysis, or qualitative examples.
Title refers to LLMs but no text-only experiments.
Theorem 4.5 is tabular NPG result from a blog, misapplied to transformers; covariance unmeasured.
Entropy explanation internally inconsistent and unfalsifiable.
Theorem 4.4 trivial and holds only before positive-only filtering.
Claim that high-advantage samples are more often clipped is not measured.
Positive-only training removes negative gradients; supporting evidence correlational from one run.
Importance ratio for off-policy replayed samples unspecified.
Higher sampling temperature changes behaviour policy; ratio mismatch unaddressed.
Advantage threshold for replay is not selective.
Repeated replay on small Geo3K may overfit; no held-out analysis.
Difficulty definition mixes hard and moderate prompts; trigger rates unreported.
Admitted hyperparameter sensitivity not studied.
Ablations shallow: one dataset, curves only, missing variants.
Exploration-only variant below GRPO suggests fragile tuning.
GRPO baseline uses symmetric clipping, unmatched to method's asymmetric clipping.
Promotional language and typos.
Unresolved references, duplicate entry, blog post as key source.
Sample taxonomy restates existing splits and is not analysed.
Related-work coverage thin.
